newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy's Di Pietro calls probe a "squalid vendetta".
newsitem.headline: Italy's Di Pietro calls probe a "squalid vendetta".

text.p: Antonio Di Pietro, the ex-magistrate whose all-out assault on corruption made him a national hero in Italy, on Saturday slammed an investigation into him as "a joke and a squalid vendetta".
"This story is a joke," Di Pietro said in a statement, his first public comment since massive police raids on his offices and homes last Friday.

"This plot organised against me and also against my former colleagues (in Milan's elite pool of anti-graft magistrates) is 'botched' and it will not be difficult to tear it to pieces," the former star magistrate said.

Revenue police raided his homes and offices on Friday to search for clues of alleged irregularities he committed while spearheading the famous "Tangentopoli" (Bribesville) probes that toppled Italy's old political guard in the early 1990s.

The raids, which left many Italians shocked and puzzled, also targeted offices of Di Pietro's business associates and lawyers and were comparable in scope and media coverage to those against the Mafia.
"Not even the worst criminal gets treated like Di Pietro," Massimo Dinoia, the former magistrate's lawyer, was quoted as saying in Rome's Il Messagero daily.

The office of Giancarlo Tarquini, chief prosecutor in the town of Brescia, ordered the raids after opening a probe into Di Pietro last month over suspicions he may have been involved in extortion and abuse of office, according to media reports.

Milan's respected newspaper Corriere della Sera reported on Saturday that Tarquini suspected Di Pietro of having "economic relations" with a Swiss-Italian banker who is at the centre of a major graft probe.

The daily also said Tarquini suspected Di Pietro of giving legal protection to Pierfrancesco Pacini Battaglia in exchange for information from the banker regarding the then-magistrate's corruption suspects.
In his statement, Di Pietro said: "Obviously I have always known that my alleged economic relations with Pacini Battaglia were a vulgar lie and a squalid vendetta".

Pacini Battaglia, who magistrates suspect led a network of corruption involving several state companies, was arrested last September in a graft scandal along with the former chairman of the state railways, Lorenzo Necci.
He was granted house arrest last Tuesday while Necci is no longer in prison.

Dinoia said on Saturday that agents had seized a number of documents -- including some he wanted to use in his defence against the latest accusations -- from Di Pietro's home near Milan. Di Pietro was not present but his wife and two small children were awakened by police, the lawyer said.
Di Pietro, who resigned as magistrate two years ago and as pubilc works minister last month, was the target of an earlier probe by Brescia magistrates into allegations of corruption.
All charges against him were dropped in that inquiry in April shortly before he was named to the cabinet.

In his November 14 letter of resignation from Prime Minister Romano Prodi's government, Di Pietro said the probe was "pigeon shoot" which he implied was part of a vendetta by defendants he exposed in his corruption probes.
